Grandpa Abdul-Rahim had an olive grove on the hillside. Its trees had been planted by his grandfather's grandfather, and their trunks were twisted like the hands of old men.

He used to tell his grandson Yamen, "This land is an amanah, a trust. We inherited it from our fathers, and we will leave it to our children."

Every autumn Yamen went with his grandfather to pick the olives, and heard from him the story of each tree: this one his father planted on the day he was born; this one held on through a whole year of thirst.

One day some strangers came to the edge of the grove, carrying papers and maps. They said, "This land is ours now. Leave it."

Grandpa said in a steady voice, "This is the land of my fathers, and it has olive trees older than all of you."

When night came, the strangers cut down three trees at the edge of the grove and left them lying on the ground.

When Yamen saw them in the morning, he cried. And Grandpa sat by their cut trunks for a long time without speaking.

Then Grandpa got up, brushed the dust off his clothes, and said, "Yamen, a tree can be cut down, but its roots stay in the ground. And so do we."

Then he walked to the village.

The men of the village gathered in the square, old and young, and said, "The grove belongs to all of us, and the land belongs to all of us."

They agreed to take turns keeping watch over the groves at night, so that no land would be left without a guard.

So every night the men kept watch at the edges of the groves, with lanterns and copies of the Quran, taking turns until dawn.

Yamen brought them tea and bread, and heard them reciting: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا﴾

Standing guard was patience: the cold of the night, eyes kept awake, and fear that did not show on their faces.

But when the strangers saw the whole village staying awake to protect its land, they did not come back on those nights.

In the spring, the people of the village brought little olive seedlings and planted them where the cut trees had stood. Yamen planted one of them with his own hand.

Grandpa said, "This one is for your children, Yamen."

The years went by, and the seedling grew, and Yamen told its story to everyone who asked about it.

Land is only kept safe by its own people — when they are patient with it, stand firm on it, and never leave it.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾

📖 Al 'Imran 200. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
